content.title: About
content.content: Organic puffed millet is a light, airy snack made by quickly heating whole millet grains under pressure until they expand. The process retains most of the grain’s nutrients, giving a mild nutty flavor and a crisp texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Millet has been cultivated for over 7,000 years and is a staple in many traditional diets.
Puffing is achieved by exposing the grains to high temperature and pressure, causing them to “pop” like popcorn.
Organic farming prohibits synthetic pesticides and fertilizers, reducing environmental impact.
Millet belongs to the same grass family as rice, wheat, and corn.
Puffed millet is often used in baby foods because of its soft texture and easy digestibility.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides slowly released energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Contains about 13 % protein, making it a valuable addition to vegetarian diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which support metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many nut‑based snacks, puffed millet is virtually fat‑free, suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Millet allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to proteins in millet, especially if they have a broader grain allergy.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Millet is naturally gluten‑free, but cross‑contamination can occur during processing; not suitable for those with celiac disease if not certified gluten‑free.

items.title: Risk of mycotoxins
items.content: Improper storage of millet can lead to mold growth and mycotoxin formation; purchase from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy puffed millet as a dry snack, mix it into granola, yogurt, or plant‑based milks, use it in baked goods, or sprinkle it over salads for extra crunch. Soaking it in milk or water softens the texture for porridge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in a sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For long‑term storage, refrigerate to prevent mold growth.
